22.02.additionalInfo: 22.01 Chong Zi and 22.02 Chong Xian are needled together using the Dao Ma technique. The reaction area of these points is associated with the lungs and the heart, and they are located in the area that represents the chest in palm diagnosis. Therefore, they have a significant impact on the chest area. Master Tung wrote that combining these points effectively treats children and upper back pain. Together, these points can release the exterior, especially in cases of wind-cold invasion (symptoms include headaches, neck pain, shoulder blade pain, aversion to cold, and a tight pulse at the Cun position on the right side). 22.05 Ling Gu and 22.04 Da Bail along with 22.01-02 Chong Zi/Xian, treat the chest and lungs. The difference between them is that 22.01-02 Chong Zi/Xian is more effective in treating disorders between the shoulder blades and is better at releasing the exterior in wind-cold conditions. Since both sets of points are located opposite each other, they can be needled together with two needles, from 22.05 Ling Gu towards 22.02 Chong Xian and from 22.04 Da Bai towards 22.01 Chong Zi, to treat lung diseases. The needling should be on the opposite side when treating pain in the Thenar eminence area. The Reaction area of these points is the sub-branch of the lungs and heart, therefor these points can treat pain due to qi and blood stagnation, mainly in the chest area. These points influence the heart and, therefore, they can treat knee disorders (points with the Reaction area of the heart can treat the knee). Palm Diagnosis The points are located in the area representing the chest in the palm diagnosis. Hu Wen Zhi Combining 22.01 Zhong Zi and 22.02 Zhong Xian forms a special effect point combination for treating back pain and chest pain. Yang Wei Channel Use 22.01-02 Chong Zi/Xian with CV-24 Cheng Jiang for a stiff neck. The Nan Jing states that the Thenar muscle can help diagnose stomach and intestinal diseases. "A blue color of the muscle indicates coldness in the stomach, and a red color indicates heat in the stomach." Clinical experience Shows that the vein is sometimes red during constipation and blue during diarrhea. Swelling of the vein may indicate intestinal inflammation. The area of these points can also be used to diagnose and treat uterine tumors by observing the veins in the point area. The larger and more swollen the veins, the more likely it is to indicate the presence of a mass in the uterus, such as uterine cancer. These points can also be used to treat uterine myoma and ovarian inflammation. Point Name Chöng [m] — double, repeat Xian [flL] — immortal For additional information, see the San Xian (II) 22.01 and Chong Zi.

22.05.additionalInfo: Needling 22.04 Da Bai to 22.01 Chong ZI In Chinese Medicine, the Lungs regulate the Qi. Therefore, in Master Tung's acupuncture, we rely heavily on Lung points to treat Qi stagnation in any form. Because of this principle, 22.05 Ling Gu and 22.04 Da Bai are arguably the most important points in Master Tung's entire system for treating Qi stagnation. Both points strongly influence the Lungs and are very often needled together. We use them for conditions involving Lung Qi deficiency or Qi stagnation. In fact, this is the primary combination in Master Tung's acupuncture for treating Qi and Blood stagnation, making it useful for an incredibly wide range of conditions. Master Tung had a very clear rule when it came to complex cases. He used to say: 'Qi and blood stagnation must be present in chronic diseases, unexplained illnesses, severe diseases, and symptoms that include pain: Now, it's crucial to understand their mechanism. Ling Gu and Da Bai do not treat blood stagnation directly. Instead, they release blood stagnation through the movement of Qi. As we know, Qi commands the blood—so by regulating the Qi, we regulate the blood flow. However, if the blood stagnation has been there so long that it has led to structural changes, like tumors, this combination isn't enough. In those cases, you want to use 77.05 to 77.07 (San Zhong), which acts on the Heart, making it much more suitable for structural masses. But for moving Qi and Blood through the channels, Ling Gu and Da Bai are your primary combination. This is why they are the absolute go-to points for treating hemiplegia. In fact, this is the exact main point combination Master Tung himself used when he famously treated the Cambodian Prime Minister, Lon Nol, for his hemiplegia. When it comes to the needling technique, there are two distinct directions depending on what you want to treat. To target disorders of the lungs, coldness and numbness of the fingers, or shoulder pain, you needle 22.04 Da Bai perpendicularly 1 to 2 cun towards 22.01 Chong Zi, and 22.05 Ling Gu perpendicularly 1 to 2 cun towards 22.02 Chong Xian. However, if your goal is to treat disorders of the spine and back, you need to needle deeper and change the target: needle Da Bai perpendicularly 2 to 3 cun towards 22.08 Wan Shun Yi, and Ling Gu perpendicularly 2 to 3 cun towards 22.09 Wan Shun Er. One last clinical pearl before we move on. Always look at the patient's hand. If you observe muscle atrophy specifically in the area of Ling Gu and Da Bai, your Palm Diagnosis is telling you there is an underlying Qi and Blood deficiency leading to that atrophy, Point Name Ling - soul, quick, intelligent, clever. Gü [ft] — bone. The character "bone" in the point's name suggests its location at the junction of the first and second metacarpal bones and its influence on the kidneys. The character "clever" in the name suggests the wide range of indications for this point and its importance.

22.07.additionalInfo: Typically, 22.07 Xia Bai is needled together with 22.06 Zhong Bai using the Dao Ma technique. This point has the same indications as 22.06 Zhong Bai but additionally affects the liver. Lai Jing-Xiong adds reaction areas of the spleen and heart to this point. Therefore, combining 22.06 Zhong Bai and 22.07 Xia Bai can treat the kidneys, lungs, liver, spleen, and heart. Of the six Bai points, 22.06 Zhong Bai and 22.07 Xia Bai are the most important. They can be used for various disorders related to kidney deficiency that affect all five Zang organs. For additional information, see 22.06 Zhong Bai. Nephrolithiasis (kidney stones) While acupuncture does not physically crush kidney stones, it is a highly effective treatment for facilitating their natural passage, provided the stones are smaller than 6 millimeters. Rather than breaking the stone, the treatment focuses on creating the optimal physiological conditions for its expulsion. It works by relaxing and dilating the smooth muscle of the ureters (spasmolysis), allowing the stone to pass without getting stuck. Additionally, acupuncture promotes diuresis, creating a natural hydraulic pressure that helps flush the system, While simultaneously reducing the local inflammation and tissue swelling that can narrow the urinary tract. Ultimately, this approach significantly relieves the severe pain of renal colic and supports the smooth, natural exit of the stone. Point Name Xiå [F] — lower. Båi - White. The character "lower" in the point's name indicates that it is located proximal to 22.06 Zhong Bai. For additional information, See 22.03 Shang Bai.

22.10.additionalInfo: Primary points for treating pain. In Chinese medicine, pain is associated with the heart, as the heart is the organ that senses pain. These points are located in an area that represents the kidney on the palm, and their reaction area is related to the sensitive nerve of the kidneys. Therefore, these points influence the heart by controlling water (kidneys) over fire (heart). Palm Diagnosis: According to palm diagnosis, the points are located in the area that represents the gallbladder. Consequently, these points also address gallbladder conditions such as cholecystitis and gallstones. The gallbladder is a unique Fu organ; unique Fu organs store essences. Thus, the gallbladder area on the palm is positioned between the pathways of the kidneys and liver. Hu wen Zhi: One of Tung's 32 points provides a solution for toxic conditions. According to Hu Wen Zhi, the point's reaction area is the sensitive nerve of the five Fu organs. When the emperor (heart) is calm, tranquility will prevail in all five Zang organs. Conversely, the emperor's (heart) restlessness will affect all five Zang organs. One or both points can be combined with Xin ling (33) For anesthesia. Point Name Shöu [+] — hand. Shöu [3] — hand. Jié [N] — to separate, divide, and release. The points' names indicate their location on the hand, as opposed to 88.28 Jie "release," which is located on the leg. The names of the points suggest their ability to release the flow of qi and blood and treat pain. Shöu [9] — hand.

22.11.additionalInfo: The points are located along the extension of the thumb, which represents the spleen. Their reaction area is associated with the spleen and kidneys, thus influencing the connection between these organs. The points strengthen the kidney yang, which supports the spleen. These points can treat conditions related to cold (kidneys) and dampness (spleen) affecting the stomach, intestines, lungs, and skeletal system. They are important for treating stomach diseases, particularly gastritis and chronic stomach conditions. The points can address lung disorders (asthma, cough, sore throat) due to spleen and kidney deficiency. Proper lung function depends on kidney yang and spleen qi. When these are weak, they fail to nourish the lungs, leading to lung deficiency. Although Master Tung indicated that these points treat finger pain, they can also address pain and swelling in the bones throughout the body, especially due to cold and dampness. Palm Diagnosis: The area of these points reflects the intestines. Lai Jing-Xiong: Used the points for weight loss. Chuan Min Wang: 22.11 Tu Shui (choose one point) combined with 22.10 Shou Jie can treat numbness and tingling in the hands and feet. Liao Li: Needling close to the bone treats knee pain. Point Name Tü — earth. Shui [7k] — water. The characters nearth" (spleen-stomach) and "water" (kidneys) in the point name suggest their influence on the spleen, stomach, and kidneys. The names also hint at their ability to treat dampness (earth) and cold (water).
